method.retriever: hybrid BM25+sqlite-vec weighted RRF with optional query expansion; reranker from AUDIT_RAG_RERANKER
method.recall_at_k_all: Fraction of answerable questions where every gold chunk_id appears in the top k retrieved chunks.
method.mean_recall_at_k: Macro-average of |gold ∩ retrieved@k| / |gold| on answerable questions.
method.mrr: Mean reciprocal rank of the first gold chunk in the retrieved list, on answerable questions.
method.doc_recall_at_k: Fraction of answerable questions where at least one gold doc_id appears in the top k.
method.citation_accuracy: On non-refusal answers, each claim sentence must have a [rank:chunk_id] marker, the chunk must be in the retrieved set, and at least half of the claim's content tokens (min 3, or all if fewer) must appear in the cited chunk. Refusals with no citations score 1.0.
method.faithfulness: Same lexical support test as citation accuracy. This is not an LLM-as-judge score and can miss valid paraphrases.
method.refusal_accuracy: (true refusals + true answers) / N, using must_refuse from the golden set.
method.refusal_rule: The extractive generator also refuses when a proper-noun or identifier token from the question is missing from the retrieved chunks, or when a question asks for an exact dollar/amount loss and the candidate answer has no currency figure. This is lexical, not an LLM judge.

records.question: What is a reentrancy attack, and what remediations does the SWC Registry recommend?
records.answer: Historically, it has often been recommended to use these functions for value transfers to guard against reentrancy attacks [4:swc-134#c0]. It is also recommended that you use replay protection (see [SWC-121](./SWC-121.md)), although an attacker can still bypass this by [front-running](./SWC-114.md) [5:swc-133#c3]. # SWC-107: Reentrancy ## Relationships [CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/841.html) ## Description One of the major dangers of calling external contracts is that they can take over the control flow [1:swc-107#c1]. ## Remediation It is not recommended to use alternate verification schemes that do not require proper signature verification through `ecrecover()` [3:swc-122#c3].

records.question: What weakness is classified as SWC-117?
records.answer: The `ecrecover` function is susceptible to signature malleability (see also SWC-117) [1:swc-121#c3]. # SWC-117: Signature Malleability [3:swc-117#c0] - [Medium - Replay Attack Vulnerability in Ethereum Smart Contracts Introduced by transferProxy()](https://medium.com/cypher-core/replay-attack-vulnerability-in-ethereum-smart-contracts-introduced-by-transferproxy-124bf3694e25) [1:swc-121#c3] The EVM specification defines several so-called ‘precompiled’ contracts one of them being `ecrecover` which executes the elliptic curve public key recovery [3:swc-117#c0].

records.question: According to not-so-smart-contracts, what should be done about variable shadowing?
records.answer: # not-so-smart-contracts: Variable Shadowing Variable shadowing occurs when a variable declared within a certain scope (decision block, method, or inner class) has the same name as a variable declared in an outer scope [1:nssc-variable-shadowing#c1]. # not-so-smart-contracts: Variable Shadowing [2:nssc-variable-shadowing#c0] This is a particularly nasty bug that is made even more insidious by the fact that the solc compiler will throw no error or warning indicating that the owner address is in fact being [shadowed](https://github.com/trailofbits/not-so-smart-contracts/tree/master/variable%20shadowing) by the inheriting `CEOThrone` contract [4:nssc-honeypots#c2]. # not-so-smart-contracts: Re-entrancy A state variable is changed after a contract uses `call.value` [5:nssc-reentrancy#c1].

citation_detail.claim: # not-so-smart-contracts: Variable Shadowing Variable shadowing occurs when a variable declared within a certain scope (decision block, method, or inner class) has the same name as a variable declared in an outer scope [1:nssc-variable-shadowing#c1].

records.question: What is SWC-128 about?
records.answer: # SWC-128: DoS With Block Gas Limit [1:swc-128#c0] # SWC-128: DoS With Block Gas Limit ## Relationships - [CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html) - EEA EthTrust Security Levels: - [**[Q] Manage Gas Usage Increases**](https://entethalliance.github.io/eta-registry/security-levels-spec.html#req-3-enough-gas) [2:swc-128#c1] - [**[Q] Manage Gas Usage Increases**](https://entethalliance.github.io/eta-registry/security-levels-spec.html#req-3-enough-gas) [1:swc-128#c0] When smart contracts are deployed or functions inside them are called, the execution of these actions always requires a certain amount of gas, based of how much computation is needed to complete them [2:swc-128#c1].
